The average two-bedroom rent in the Toronto CMA was **$2,045 a month** in the October 2025 CMHC Rental Market Survey. That is **$73 (+3.7%) higher** than the $1,972 recorded in October 2024.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 34-10-0133-01, vector v3823103. The series is Toronto, Ontario; row and apartment structures of three units and over; two-bedroom units. The values are in nominal dollars.
- **Reference periods:** 2025 is $2,045 and 2024 is $1,972. The survey is taken in the first two weeks of October and labelled with its year.
- **Quality:** Both values carry a normal status flag. The table was released 2025-12-17.
- **Scope:** This figure covers the survey's whole universe of structures with three or more units. CMHC's own apartment-only (six units and over) figures differ.

I calculated the change myself from the two published values. I did not pull a separate CMHC-published percentage.

The vacancy rate for purpose-built rental units (row and apartment structures of three or more units) in the Toronto CMA was **3.0% in October 2025**. That is up from **1.4% in October 2023**, a rise of 1.6 percentage points, so the rate is more than double.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 34-10-0130-01, vector v1930324, which republishes CMHC's Rental Market Survey. The survey is taken in early October and labelled with its year.
- **Other years in the series:** 2022 was 1.6% and 2024 was 2.5%. The rate has risen each year since 2023.
- **Table choice:** Table 34-10-0127-01 covers apartment structures of six or more units only, and its rates differ. I used 34-10-0130-01 because it covers the survey's whole universe.
- **Geography:** CMA boundaries are revised every five years, so comparisons across census periods are not strictly like-for-like.

In October 2025, the average two-bedroom rent in the Oshawa CMA was $283 a month lower than in the Toronto CMA.

| CMA | Average two-bedroom rent, Oct 2025 | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| Oshawa | $1,762 | v3823091 |
| Toronto | $2,045 | v3823103 |

- Oshawa's rent was about 14% below Toronto's ($283 ÷ $2,045).
- Oshawa rents rose 4.3% from 2024 ($1,690 to $1,762). Toronto rents rose 3.7% ($1,972 to $2,045).
- The source is Statistics Canada table 34-10-0133-01, which republishes the CMHC Rental Market Survey. The reference period is the 2025 survey, taken in early October and labelled 2025.
- The figures cover row and apartment structures of three or more units, in current dollars.
- Oshawa is the CMA that covers Durham's urban core. The data is not for Durham Region as a whole.

**Oshawa had the highest rental vacancy rate of the three in 2025, at 3.6%.**

| CMA | 2025 vacancy rate | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| Oshawa | 3.6% | v1930312 |
| Hamilton | 3.5% | v1930306 |
| Toronto | 3.0% | v1930324 |

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 34-10-0130-01, which republishes CMHC's Rental Market Survey. Reference period is 2025 (the October 2025 survey). Table released 2025-12-17.
- **Coverage:** Privately initiated row and apartment structures of three or more units (weighted average).
- **Margin:** Oshawa and Hamilton are only 0.1 percentage point apart. I didn't check CMHC's reliability flags, so treat that gap as close to a tie.
- **Other structure types:** Table 34-10-0127-01 covers apartment structures of six or more units only, and its rates differ. I didn't check it.

Toronto CMA housing starts fell about 31% from 2024 to 2025:

| Year | Total housing starts (units) |
|---|---|
| 2025 | **26,087** |
| 2024 | **37,718** |

The change is −11,631 units, or about −30.8% (my calculation).

**Sources**
- **2025:** Statistics Canada table 34-10-0134-01 (annual), vector v42127955, reference period 2025. The figure is 26,087 and carries no quality flag. The 2025 monthly values in table 34-10-0154-01, vector v42127475, sum to the same 26,087.
- **2024:** The annual table 34-10-0134-01 has no published value for 2024 or 2023. Its status reads "not available for a specific reference period". I summed the 12 monthly values for January to December 2024 in table 34-10-0154-01 (vector v42127475) to get 37,718.
- **Comparability:** Both years are CMHC Starts and Completions Survey data for the Toronto CMA, "Total units". The 2024 total is my sum and is not a published annual figure. StatCan notes that CMA boundaries are updated every five years, which may be why the annual table has gaps.

New home prices in the Toronto CMA fell about 3.4% between December 2024 and December 2025. The source is the New Housing Price Index (NHPI), Statistics Canada table 18-10-0205-01, index 2016-12=100. The index tracks price changes, not dollar price levels.

| Series (vector) | Dec 2024 | Dec 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total, house and land (v111955499) | 113.1 | 109.3 | **-3.4%** |
| House only (v111955500) | 111.9 | 106.4 | -4.9% |
| Land only (v111955501) | 114.9 | 115.2 | +0.3% |

- **Trend:** The total index drifted down through 2025, from 112.6 in January to 109.3 in December.
- **Land only:** Statistics Canada flags these values "use with caution" (quality code E).
- **Percentages:** I calculated them from the published index values.

A year of average two-bedroom rent in Toronto would take about **28.7%** of the Toronto CMA's median after-tax income in 2024.

- **Rent:** $1,972 a month in October 2024, or $23,664 over 12 months. This is the average for two-bedroom units in row and apartment structures of three or more units. Source: Statistics Canada table 34-10-0133-01, vector v3823103, reference period 2024 (CMHC Rental Market Survey, taken in October).
- **Income:** $82,500 in 2024 constant dollars. This is the median after-tax income of economic families and persons not in an economic family. Source: Statistics Canada table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96415851, reference period 2024.
- **Calculation:** $23,664 ÷ $82,500 = 28.7%.

- **Unit of income:** The income figure covers each family, or each person living alone or with non-relatives, as one unit. It is not a per-person or per-household figure, and a per-person median would be much lower.
- **Rent basis:** The rent is an October snapshot of what tenants pay in purpose-built rental units. It leaves out condos and other secondary-market rentals, which often cost more.

Toronto CMA two-bedroom rents rose about 26% from 2019 to 2024. Median after-tax income rose only about 2%, but the two figures are in different dollars, so they aren't strictly comparable.

| Measure | 2019 | 2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average two-bedroom rent, Toronto CMA (current dollars; Oct. survey, row and apartment structures of 3+ units) | $1,563 | $1,972 | **+26.2%** |
| Median after-tax income, Toronto CMA (2024 constant dollars; economic families and persons not in an economic family) | $80,800 | $82,500 | **+2.1%** (real) |

- **Rent:** Statistics Canada table 34-10-0133-01, vector v3823103, reference periods 2019 and 2024. The data comes from the CMHC Rental Market Survey.
- **Income:** Statistics Canada table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96415851, reference years 2019 and 2024.
- **Mismatch:** Rent is in nominal dollars and income is in inflation-adjusted dollars, so the gap is not strictly like-for-like. I did not retrieve a CPI series or a nominal after-tax income series, so I haven't converted either figure.
- **Income unit:** The income figure is per economic family or person living alone. It is not per household or per individual.
- **Rent measure:** The rent change is the gap between two years' average rents. It includes the effect of new and changed units in the sample, so it isn't CMHC's same-structure rent change.
- **Income revisions:** The 2018–2023 income estimates were revised in 2026 to reflect 2021 Census counts.
- **Income survey:** The 2022 methodology changes may affect comparisons between 2019 and 2024.

The 2025 average two-bedroom rent in the Toronto CMA is about **25.3% of 2021 Census median household income**.

- **Rent:** $2,045 a month in October 2025. This is the CMHC Rental Market Survey average for row and apartment structures of three or more units. Source: Statistics Canada table 34-10-0133-01, vector v3823103, reference period 2025.
- **Annual rent:** $2,045 × 12 = $24,540.
- **Income:** $97,000, the median total household income in the Toronto CMA. Source: 2021 Census Profile, characteristic 229, geography 2021S0503535. The Census Profile gives no table or vector ID. The reference period is income year 2020.
- **Share:** $24,540 ÷ $97,000 ≈ 25.3%.

- **Mismatched years:** The income is from 2020 and the rent is from 2025, so the share is overstated compared with today's incomes. I did not adjust for income growth.
- **Different geography from the city:** Both figures are for the Toronto CMA, not the City of Toronto alone.
- **Different population:** The rent is the average for CMHC-surveyed units. The income is for all households, owners included.

Toronto rents rose faster than overall consumer prices in 2025. Rented accommodation went up 3.1%, against 1.8% for all items.

These are calendar-year annual average changes, from Statistics Canada table 18-10-0005-01 (CPI, annual average, not seasonally adjusted, 2002=100). I calculated the percentages from the published indexes.

| Toronto series | Vector | 2024 | 2025 | Annual change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rented accommodation | v41695188 | 158.6 | 163.5 | **+3.1%** |
| All-items | v41695186 | 164.7 | 167.7 | **+1.8%** |

Rents rose about 1.3 percentage points faster than overall prices. The CPI rent index measures price change for rented accommodation in the Toronto CPI area. It is not the average rent paid.

In 2025, shelter inflation in Toronto was lower than in Canada as a whole. Toronto's annual average was up 2.1% and Canada's was up 3.0%, a gap of about 0.9 percentage points.

| Geography | Shelter CPI, 2024 | Shelter CPI, 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Toronto | 187.3 | 191.3 | **+2.1%** |
| Canada | 182.3 | 187.8 | **+3.0%** |

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 18-10-0005-01, Consumer Price Index, annual average, not seasonally adjusted (2002=100). The reference period is calendar-year 2025, from the release of 2026-01-19.
- **Vectors:** Toronto is v41695187 and Canada is v41693348.
- **Method:** I calculated the percent changes from the published, rounded annual-average indexes. They are not December-to-December changes.
- **Context:** Toronto's shelter inflation slowed more sharply than Canada's. In 2024 it was 5.9% in Toronto against 5.7% nationally.

I did not break shelter down into rent versus owned accommodation or mortgage interest cost. Mortgage interest cost is published for Canada only, not for Toronto.

In August 2026, Toronto shelter prices were slightly lower than a year earlier, while overall consumer prices were higher.

| Toronto, August 2026 | Index (2002=100) | Aug 2025 | Year over year |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shelter (v41692889) | 190.5 | 191.4 | **−0.5%** |
| All-items (v41692888) | 171.7 | 168.1 | **+2.1%** |

Shelter prices therefore rose about 2.6 percentage points more slowly than the overall index.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 18-10-0004-01, Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted. Both series are for Toronto, Ontario, for the reference period August 2026.
- **Calculation:** I computed the percentages from the published, rounded index values (190.5/191.4 and 171.7/168.1). Statistics Canada's own published rate of change could differ by 0.1 point.
- **Trend:** Toronto shelter has been below its year-earlier level every month since January 2026, ranging from −0.2% to −1.0%.
- **Scope:** Statistics Canada publishes only six CPI series for Toronto, and this shelter series is one of them. Shelter sub-components such as mortgage interest cost are not published at the city level.

The Bank of Canada changed its policy rate **4 times in 2025**, and every change was a cut of 0.25 percentage points. The data is the Bank of Canada Valet series V39079, the target for the overnight rate (the policy rate).

- **Start of the year:** 3.25%, on 2025-01-01 (set on 2024-12-12).
- **End of the year:** 2.25%, on 2025-12-31.

The four cuts:

| Date | Rate |
|---|---|
| 2025-01-30 | 3.25% to 3.00% |
| 2025-03-13 | 3.00% to 2.75% |
| 2025-09-18 | 2.75% to 2.50% |
| 2025-10-30 | 2.50% to 2.25% |

The rate was held at 2.75% from March until mid-September. It was unchanged from the October cut through year-end.

The Bank of Canada series is the source for all of this. Statistics Canada tables and vectors don't apply here.

I couldn't find a Toronto figure for mortgage interest cost inflation in 2025, because Statistics Canada doesn't publish one.

Mortgage interest cost is published for Canada as a whole only. For Toronto, the CPI tables (18-10-0004-01 monthly, 18-10-0005-01 annual average) carry just six series:
- All-items
- Shelter
- Rented accommodation
- Owned accommodation
- Water, fuel and electricity
- All-items (1992=100)

I haven't given a number, since any Toronto mortgage-interest figure would be an estimate.

I can pull one of these instead:
- **National mortgage interest cost**, 2025 annual average change, from 18-10-0005-01.
- **Toronto owned accommodation or shelter**, 2025, as the closest city-level measures.

Tell me which you want.

I checked the series and I'm giving the result now.

**I can't give a 1985 figure, because the data doesn't exist in these tables.**

- The Statistics Canada series for Toronto two-bedroom average rent is table 34-10-0133-01, vector v3823103. It covers row and apartment structures of three or more units in the Toronto CMA, and it comes from the CMHC Rental Market Survey.
- The table starts in 1987. For Toronto two-bedroom units, the values for 1987 to 1991 are marked "not available for a specific reference period". The first published value is 1992.
- I didn't estimate 1985 by back-casting.

**Nearest published figure:** $755 in October 1992, in current dollars (v3823103, 34-10-0133-01). That is seven years after your target year, so it isn't a substitute for 1985.

For 1985 itself, you could look at CMHC's older Rental Market Survey publications or the 1986 Census. I haven't checked either, so I can't say whether they hold a comparable Toronto two-bedroom figure.
